body:
## Problem
`pdca split --accept` files the children as GitHub sub-issues and leaves the parent open. The instance rule ("parents stay open as seam trackers") turned every split into N+1 open issues: in the Wyrd instance #508, #635, #636, #637, #654, #692, #717 and #735 are all open parents whose scope is entirely in children, and the milestone view counts them as work. Three-level splits happened (#654 → #692 → #717 → #771/#772).

Evidence: getwyrd/wyrd-pdca `docs/2026-09-11-backlog-reversal-proposal.md` (§1, §2 deltas 2–3).

## Proposal
On `split --accept`:
- close the parent tracker issue with a comment listing the children (the parent bundle already freezes at COMPLETE with `close: no PR`), **or** if the tracker supports it, mark it a container so it does not count as open work — pick per `[tracker]` capability, default to close;
- record `split_depth` in the child bundle's notes (parent depth + 1) and refuse `split --accept` at depth ≥ 2 without `--force`, so a slice is split at most once by default.

## Acceptance
- After `split --accept` the parent issue is CLOSED (or container-marked) and the comment names every child.
- `split --accept` on a depth-2 bundle exits non-zero without `--force`.
title: split --accept: close the parent tracker issue and bound split depth
